findings.highlight: wasn't something I could see, but something I could smell
findings.evidenceJa: 見えるものと言うよりは染みるものだった
findings.explanation: The smoke is less something Haruki can see than something that stings or smartingly gets into his eyes, as the tears on the next line confirm. The translation changes that physical eye irritation into smell.
findings.japanese:
俺が部屋に飛び込んだとき真っ先に目に入ったのは、
見えるものと言うよりは染みるものだったりした。
findings.todokanai: The first sensation that came to me the moment I bolted into the room wasn't something I could see, but something I could smell.

findings.highlight: finish the first and second movements today
findings.evidenceJa: 今日中に、二曲目までは完成させる
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will finish through the second piece today. 曲 refers to separate pieces in the concert program, not the first and second movements of one work.
findings.japanese:
「今日中に、二曲目までは完成させる。
三日前までには完璧にしておくよ」
findings.todokanai: "I'll finish the first and second movements today. I'll have everything done completely three days before the concert."

findings.highlight: for that in itself was part of her ability
findings.evidenceJa: それでいて実力も一流だったから
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that despite promoting herself beyond what her ability alone warranted, Youko's actual ability was also first-rate. The English redefines promotion as part of her ability and deletes the concession that she truly was a first-rate pianist.
findings.japanese:
「実力以上に人気を獲得する手段をよく知ってた。
一応、それでいて実力も一流だったから、
誰も文句は言えなかった」
findings.todokanai: "She was very good at getting popularity above what her actual ability warranted. Though I suppose no one could complain, for that in itself was part of her ability."

findings.highlight: she crushed them all with shady tactics
findings.evidenceJa: 全部実力と裏工作で叩き潰してきた
findings.explanation: Youko crushed her complainers and rivals with both genuine skill and backstage maneuvering. Omitting 実力 makes her success rest entirely on dirty tricks, contradicting Kazusa's deliberately mixed respect and contempt.
findings.japanese:
「…いいや、文句を言ったり、
妬んだりする人間はたくさんいたけど、
全部実力と裏工作で叩き潰してきた」
findings.todokanai: "…No, there were plenty of people who complained about her and envied her, but she crushed them all with shady tactics."

findings.highlight: I can't reach that castle of hers.
findings.evidenceJa: あの域に達するのは不可能だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot reach that level—the extreme domain of Youko's sexual and promotional tactics. 域 is a level or realm, not a castle.
findings.japanese:
「あたしにはできない…
あの域に達するのは不可能だ」
findings.todokanai: "It's something I'm incapable of… I can't reach that castle of hers."

findings.highlight: I haven't lost my way yet.
findings.evidenceJa: 少なくとも軸はぶれてないからな
findings.explanation: Haruki defends Youko by saying that at least her underlying axis or guiding purpose has never wavered. The translation makes Haruki claim that he himself has not lost his way.
findings.japanese:
「少なくとも軸はぶれてないからな。
それに俺だって本人には言いたいこと言ってる」
findings.todokanai: "I haven't lost my way yet. And besides, I'm only saying what I want to tell her myself."

findings.highlight: with the help of a single female worker
findings.evidenceJa: 女手一つでこんなワガママ娘を育てた
findings.explanation: 女手一つで means Youko raised her daughter single-handedly as a woman or single mother. The translation invents a separate female employee who helped her raise Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
「当たり前だ。
そうやって女手一つでこんなワガママ娘を育てたんだ。
どこに嫌われる理由があるんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Of course not. She raised such a spoiled daughter with the help of a single female worker. Why would you ever hate her?"

findings.highlight: converting this to a book or a movie script
findings.evidenceJa: 書籍化した方がいいかもしれないな
findings.explanation: Hamada suggests turning the material into a book. A movie script is entirely absent and changes his publishing-industry proposal into an additional adaptation plan.
findings.japanese:
「………書籍化した方がいいかもしれないな。
今出せば『今週のベストセラー』くらいなら
余裕で狙える」
findings.todokanai: "…We might be better off converting this to a book or a movie script. I'm sure we'd be able to produce the bestseller of the week with this."

findings.highlight: It's not like I can just say no
findings.evidenceJa: 断ることもできたんだけどね
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly says she could have refused the business trip, but accepted because it was the opportunity she had long requested and refusal might cost future work. The translation says she could not simply refuse, removing her active career choice.
findings.japanese:
「断ることもできたんだけどね…
でも、ずっと希望してたし、なのに断っちゃうと、
二度とこういう仕事回ってこないかもって」
findings.todokanai: "It's not like I can just say no… but I always hoped for something like this. If I said no now, I might never get a chance for a job like this again."

findings.highlight: there was this independent conductor
findings.evidenceJa: 一人傑作なのがいてさ。フランス人の、３０半ばの指揮者で
findings.explanation: Kazusa says there was one especially outrageous or hilarious specimen, a French conductor in his mid-thirties. 一人 counts the person and 傑作 marks him as a piece of work; it does not mean an independent conductor.
findings.japanese:
「で、一人傑作なのがいてさ。
フランス人の、３０半ばの指揮者で…
そいつ、若い頃母さんの愛人やってたらしいんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Anyway, there was this independent conductor. A Frenchman in his mid thirties… Apparently he was mom's lover when he was young."

findings.highlight: she looks sorrowful as if hit with a painful realization
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱり痛快でどうしようもないみたいに
findings.explanation: Kazusa finds Haruki's visible relief irresistibly satisfying or exhilarating because she is teasing his jealousy. The translation reverses her delight into sorrow and a painful realization.
findings.japanese:
俺が、ほっとした表情を浮かべるのも、
やっぱり痛快でどうしようもないみたいに。
findings.todokanai: And when I breathe a sigh of relief in the end, she looks sorrowful as if hit with a painful realization.

findings.highlight: a standing member of the Paris orchestra
findings.evidenceJa: 今でもパリのオケの常任だよ
findings.explanation: The man is still a permanent or resident conductor of a Paris orchestra. He is not merely a standing rank-and-file orchestra member.
findings.japanese:
「そいつ、今でもパリのオケの常任だよ。
なんなら名前も教えようか？
もしかしたらあたしの父親かも」
findings.todokanai: "He's still a standing member of the Paris orchestra. Should I tell you his name? He might even be my father."

findings.highlight: tons of men who had as little talent as they had money
findings.evidenceJa: 金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、当てはまる奴らばっかりだった
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the same two categories apply if 'money' is replaced with 'talent': men too talented to care about her and untalented men whose pride cannot bear her. The translation collapses that mirrored binary into uniformly poor, untalented men.
findings.japanese:
「ああ、そうだ…
金の代わりに才能って置き換えても、
当てはまる奴らばっかりだった」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, right… there were tons of men who had as little talent as they had money."

findings.highlight: platonic physical intimacy
findings.evidenceJa: ただスキンシップを重ねただけ。俺の欲求を一方的に満たしただけ
findings.explanation: Haruki says he merely accumulated physical contact and one-sidedly satisfied his desire. Adding 'platonic' sanitizes contact that the surrounding narration explicitly frames as taboo, self-gratifying, and escalating sexual desire.
findings.japanese:
ただスキンシップを重ねただけ。
俺の欲求を一方的に満たしただけ。
findings.todokanai: All I did was initiate some platonic physical intimacy. I only managed to gratify my own desires one-sidedly.

findings.highlight: turn 30 and suddenly kick the bucket
findings.evidenceJa: ３０過ぎていきなりキたら嫌だなぁ
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that the consequences of this workload will suddenly hit or catch up with him after thirty. The translation escalates delayed burnout or bodily collapse into sudden death.
findings.japanese: …３０過ぎていきなりキたら嫌だなぁ。
findings.todokanai: …I wouldn't want to turn 30 and suddenly kick the bucket.

findings.highlight: It's not commendable, but I won't be able to do any interviews today.
findings.evidenceJa: とてもじゃないけど、今日は取材はできない
findings.explanation: とてもじゃないけど means there is simply no way he can conduct an interview this late. It is not a moral judgment that interviewing would be uncommendable.
findings.japanese:
時計を見ると、午前０時をとっくに過ぎてる。
とてもじゃないけど、今日は取材はできない。
findings.todokanai: Looking at the clock I see that it's long past midnight. It's not commendable, but I won't be able to do any interviews today.

findings.highlight: my dishonesty in skipping our interview without calling her
findings.evidenceJa: 不誠実を働いた『ことになってる』昨夜
findings.explanation: The scare-quoted ことになってる says last night is being treated as though Haruki dishonestly skipped an interview without notice; Haruki disputes that premise because he only promised to call when coming. The English states the dishonesty as fact and drops the scene's argumentative frame.
findings.japanese:
俺が連絡もせずに取材をすっぽかすという、
不誠実を働いた『ことになってる』昨夜についての…
findings.todokanai: She's been babbling about my dishonesty in skipping our interview without calling her about it last night…

findings.highlight: All the articles must be published by Friday
findings.evidenceJa: 記事の提出期限は金曜朝まで
findings.explanation: Friday morning is the deadline for Haruki to submit the article, not the publication date for multiple articles. The distinction matters to Kazusa's argument that he still had one or two days of scheduling slack.
findings.japanese:
「…記事の提出期限は金曜朝までだから、
まぁ、１、２日は余裕あったけど」
findings.todokanai: "…All the articles must be published by Friday, though I suppose I had a day or two to spare."

findings.highlight: Those two hours reminiscing about some family-centered soap opera
findings.evidenceJa: そんな、ホームドラマというかフィクションみたいな二時間
findings.explanation: The warm two-hour visit itself felt like a family drama or fiction. They were not spending the two hours reminiscing about a soap opera; the genre label is Haruki's metaphor for the improbable reunion.
findings.japanese:
そんな、ホームドラマというか
フィクションみたいな二時間は、
あっという間に過ぎ去った。
findings.todokanai: Those two hours reminiscing about some family-centered soap opera felt like they went by in a flash.

findings.highlight: eventually from even herself
findings.evidenceJa: とうとう自分からも距離を置いてしまったとき
findings.explanation: Within the indirect account of Mrs. Shibata's apology, 自分 is Mrs. Shibata: Kazusa eventually distanced herself even from her. The translation instead says Kazusa distanced herself from herself, inventing psychological self-alienation and removing Shibata from her own regret.
findings.japanese:
かずさが世間からドロップアウトして、
ピアノも捨てて、周囲からどんどん距離を置き、
とうとう自分からも距離を置いてしまったとき…
findings.todokanai: Back when Kazusa shut herself off from society, abandoning even the piano. When she distanced herself more and more from her surroundings, and eventually from even herself…

findings.highlight: her happy memories and her painful memories might have just been mixed up
findings.evidenceJa: 楽しかった思い出や、辛かった記憶が余計にデフォルメされただけ
findings.explanation: Haruki considers whether five years have further exaggerated or distorted Shibata's happy and painful memories. He does not suggest that the two categories became confused or mixed together.
findings.japanese:
旦那さんも、最近涙もろくなってきたと言っていた。
あれから五年経って、楽しかった思い出や、
辛かった記憶が余計にデフォルメされただけかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: Her husband told me she's been tearing up quite a lot recently. After five years, her happy memories and her painful memories might have just been mixed up.

findings.highlight: I don't think she's wrong in doing so.
findings.evidenceJa: そのことを間違ってるなんて思っていない
findings.explanation: Haruki believes his own ambush was worthy of criticism but does not believe that doing it was wrong. The translation instead says Kazusa is not wrong to criticize him, replacing his moral defense of the act with agreement about her response.
findings.japanese:
俺は非難されるにふさわしい騙し討ちをしたし、
そしてそのことを間違ってるなんて思っていないから。
findings.todokanai: I did plan a surprise attack worthy of criticism, and I don't think she's wrong in doing so.

findings.highlight: before it was just our fingers that were intertwined
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまで指が触れていただけだったのに
findings.explanation: Until that moment their fingers had merely been touching; now their palms meet, and only on the following lines do all their fingers interlace. The translation moves interlacing earlier and breaks the staged escalation of contact.
findings.japanese:
だって、さっきまで指が触れていただけだったのに、
今は、手のひらを合わせてる。
findings.todokanai: Because before it was just our fingers that were intertwined, but now I can feel her entire palm.

findings.highlight: …That question, along with the warmth and sweat of Kazusa's palm, dissipates into nothingness.
findings.evidenceJa:
…そんな問いかけは、
かずさの手のひらの、あまりの熱さと汗に、
かき消されてしまった。
findings.explanation: Haruki's questions are drowned out by the extraordinary heat and sweat of Kazusa's palm; the English says the physical sensations dissipate along with the question — Their contact still overwhelms his moral reasoning.
findings.japanese:
…そんな問いかけは、
かずさの手のひらの、あまりの熱さと汗に、
かき消されてしまった。
findings.todokanai: …That question, along with the warmth and sweat of Kazusa's palm, dissipates into nothingness.

findings.highlight: When I saw that they put Touma Kazusa's image on the advertisements for the school
findings.evidenceJa: 発売後、『我が校』の写真に冬馬かずさ本人が写り込んでるのを見たら
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines Suwa, after the publication goes on sale, discovering Kazusa herself in a photograph of 'our school.' The English makes Haruki the past-tense viewer and turns the future magazine photo into school advertising.
findings.japanese:
発売後、『我が校』の写真に
冬馬かずさ本人が写り込んでるのを見たら…
ま、クレームがないことを祈ろう。
findings.todokanai: When I saw that they put Touma Kazusa's image on the advertisements for the school… I can only pray she doesn't file charges.

findings.highlight: I'm savoring the experience until the concert.
findings.evidenceJa: コンサートまで、お預けだ
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Haruki that hearing her play is withheld from him until the concert—he must wait. The English makes Kazusa herself voluntarily savor an experience, reversing who is being denied.
findings.japanese:
「この前も言っただろ？
コンサートまで、お預けだ」
findings.todokanai: "Didn't I tell you earlier? I'm savoring the experience until the concert."

findings.highlight: our memories after this point diverge
findings.evidenceJa: ここから俺の記憶は途切れる
findings.explanation: Haruki's memory simply cuts out from this point because he fell asleep. The translation invents a divergence between two people's memories, obscuring why only Kazusa can narrate the unseen interval.
findings.japanese: だから、ここから俺の記憶は途切れる。
findings.todokanai: Because of that, our memories after this point diverge.

findings.highlight: making love to him
findings.evidenceJa: キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。…そいつのこと好きになったのも
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she was first to kiss him, embrace him, and fall in love with him. 抱きあった is mutual embracing, not sex; 'making love' invents an impossible sexual encounter while Haruki was asleep and corrupts the revelation's exact hierarchy of firsts.
findings.japanese:
「キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。
…そいつのこと好きになったのも」
findings.todokanai: "Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."

findings.highlight: Even if it's only spam mail
findings.evidenceJa: それがスパムメールだったとしても
findings.explanation: Haruki says even if the interruption had been spam, its timing would have been uncannily exact; the next line reveals it is from Setsuna. 'It's only spam mail' falsely identifies the actual message as spam.
findings.japanese:
それがスパムメールだったとしても、
あまりにも絶妙で、ピンポイントで、
最高にして最悪のタイミングだったけれど。
findings.todokanai: Even if it's only spam mail, the timing of which it was sent was far too miraculous and precise, and it was both great and awful at the same time.

findings.highlight: You really don't know how to spot a joke.
findings.evidenceJa: お前、本当に融通利かないのな
findings.explanation: Kazusa calls Haruki rigid, inflexible, or impossible to negotiate with after he refuses her attempted final transgression. She does not claim he lacks the ability to recognize humor; her 'joke' is an admitted cover story no one believes.
findings.japanese:
「結局、最後の最後まで失敗続きだったけどな。
…お前、本当に融通利かないのな」
findings.todokanai: "Although, it failed completely until the very end… You really don't know how to spot a joke."

findings.highlight: making love to him
findings.evidenceJa: キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。…そいつのこと好きになったのも
findings.explanation: The later verbatim recollection repeats the same embrace, and the translation repeats the same invented claim that Kazusa and Haruki had sex.
findings.japanese:
『キスしたのも、抱きあったのも。
…そいつのこと好きになったのも』
findings.todokanai: "Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."

findings.highlight: One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other.
findings.evidenceJa: 熱くしたり冷たくしたり、自分でもやってることがぶれてる
findings.explanation: Haruki alternately heats and cools himself—alcohol inflames him, then cold tea attempts to cool him. The tea itself is not alternately prepared hot and cold.
findings.japanese:
熱くしたり冷たくしたり、
自分でもやってることがぶれてるとは思うけど。
findings.todokanai: One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other. Even I think my actions are not making sense.

findings.highlight: My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.
findings.evidenceJa: 揺れる心が本能に及ぼす作用が恨めしい
findings.explanation: Haruki resents the effect his wavering heart has on his bodily instincts—the arousal and masturbation made explicit by the following lines. The English makes the heart itself the experiencer of hatred and invents actions taken against instinct.
findings.japanese:
自分に起きた、心と体の反応が恐ろしい。
揺れる心が本能に及ぼす作用が恨めしい。
findings.todokanai: The response from my mind and body is terrifying. My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.
